text.text_excerpt: The place is great and only destined to get better with time. Who wouldn't want to drink beer in an old movie theater?? The beer was pretty solid as well and I am darn picky about my beer. We tried it out one night and then we were drawn back for the cask tapping at lunch time the next day. We took the owners advice and brought lunch in since there is no food. Though two days in a row there was something set up that looked like you get food and then offer a tip for it. I don't know how long that will be happening so I wouldn't stake my hunger on it. The Mega Scops was by far my favorite of the current selection of beers. I thought just about every beer was one I could drink several of tho...

Having been to all the breweries in town, I judge them on the following: 1) do I like the beers? 2) is it a place I'd like to hang out for a while and is it comfortable? 3) is it kid friendly and are there things for the kids to do? 4) can I take my dog to sleep next to us while we hang out? Wayward Owl meets ALL the requirements, like above and beyond. The beers were good. I got a flight of 4 for $8 and I liked 3 out of 4. It was a great place to hang with lots of comfy seating. It's In an old movie theatre so it's not too hot or cold. There are tons of board games and shuffleboard for the whole family. There were a couple dogs there while we were there. I am so excited about the ever expanding brewery scene in this town. What do you get when you cross a converted theater and craft beer? You get Wayward Owl Brewing with their assortment of tasty brews in a fantastic atmosphere. I love the laid back feel of this place- lots of room, a cool vibe and, of course delicious beer. Wayward is new, but they are doing a great job at producing quality beer that I really enjoyed. On the day I was here, I was able to sample a few of the beers and I think my favorite was the IPA.
